drafted_from: tools/keep-each-accounts-setup-access-request-in-a-book (from-an-older-version/src/setup-access-records.mjs.held, its README and the held test)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-each-accounts-setup-access-request-in-a-book with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"}, label \"setup-access.json:acme\" and the request {\"status\": \"draft\", \"steps\": 1}." It keeps that request in its own book and reads it back.
no_lists_because: It names no list of its own: each request is kept in its own book in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the books are kept and how the store is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-each-accounts-setup-access-request-in-a-book" with store, the label (it starts with setup-access.json) and the request.
3. The first run makes one book per label once and proves the writes on the example labels: every expected outcome and answer must match, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run writes the request to its own book at the identity you read, or refuses it and says the current identity, and reads the book back.

worked_examples.title: A new account's setup request kept in its own book
worked_examples.ask: Keep the setup request for acme as a draft with one step.

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found no book for acme, so the write has no expected identity; the prove step matched every expected outcome and answer.
worked_examples.hands_back: outcome kept, with the identity v1 and the value status draft with one step.

worked_examples.title: A write on a stale identity is refused
worked_examples.ask: Mark the acme setup ready, from the draft I read earlier.

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The book for acme holds identity v1, so the expected identity v0 is stale.
worked_examples.hands_back: outcome refused, with the reason that the kept value differs, and identity v1 so the request can be read and written again.
